body.statement: For every \(P\in\mathcal D_{L,\kappa}\) with arm-cell vector \(\mu\), the sharp identified set for \(H\) is \([H_-(\mu),H_+(\mu)]\), where \(H_-(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}(\ell_d-a_d)_+\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\min(u_d,\max(\ell_d,a_d))\}\) and \(H_+(\mu)=\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}b_d\}/\{\sum_{d=1}^{L}\max(\ell_d,b_d)\}\). Both endpoints and every interior value are attainable, and the endpoints require \(O(L)\) arithmetic operations.
body.justification: A closed form makes the unidentified-denominator target usable for comparative statics, diagnostics, and inference.
body.gap: Kroft--Mourifi\'e--Vayalinkal Theorem 1(iii) already gives sharp closed-form weighted aggregate LCDE bounds, and de Aguas, Krumscheid, Pensar, and Biele give sharp benefit and harm bounds across ordered outcome categories. The distinct object here is harm within latent same-layer stayers under selectively observed protocol-assigned selection tiers: both its numerator and denominator are unidentified, and its sharp ratio endpoints arise by contraction of the joint prism.
body.consumer: Bounds software for protocol-controlled tier-upgrade experiments can compute sharp multilayer harm endpoints in time linear in the number of layers.
